detail.text: Not decomposed, by choice. Cor 2.3 is a named statement and could be a hole, but the only named inputs beyond it are about f_t, the real function with C(f_t(m), m) = t (the binomial coefficient continued to real n through the Gamma function): Prop 2.1 bounds f_t, f_t' and f_t''. Stating those faithfully needs that definition on the record first, and the step from the nearby-solution hypothesis to m ≥ n^{9/10} is a lemma extracted from the proof of Prop 1.10, not a stated result, so a hole for i…

route.text: Decompose Prop 1.10 (Kane-type estimate) along its proof in MRSTT §2: derivative estimates for f_t (Prop 2.1), Lemma 2.2 on integer values of a function with small second derivative, Corollary 2.3 (at most one other solution with m' ∈ [m - m^{ε/10}, m] when m ≥ n^{1/2+ε}), and the step that turns the nearby-solution hypothesis into m ≥ n^{9/10}.

terminal_goal_state.text: ⊢ ∃ a₂, ∀ a ≥ a₂, ∀ (n k : ℕ), [interior solution (n,k) of a] → {n' | ∃ k', 1 ≤ k' ∧ k' < k ∧ n < n' ∧ 2 * k' ≤ n' ∧ n'.choose k' = a ∧ |↑n - ↑n'| + |↑k - ↑k'| ≤ Real.exp (Real.log (Real.log ↑a) ^ (9 / 10))}.ncard ≤ 1

references.note: Proposition 1.10 (Kane-type estimate): for ε > 0 and (n,m) a solution of C(n,m) = t in the left half, there is at most one other solution (n',m') with m' < m, n' > n and |m − m'| + |n − n'| ≪ exp((log log t)^{1−ε}). Proved in §2 by Kane's Taylor-expansion method, viewing n as an analytic function of m at fixed t (two derivatives).
references.title: K. Matomäki, M. Radziwiłł, X. Shao, T. Tao, J. Teräväinen, Singmaster's conjecture in the interior of Pascal's triangle, Quart. J. Math. 73 (2022) 1137–1177

literature_proposed.summary: Known (2022), not formalised. This hole is Proposition 1.10 of Matomäki–Radziwiłł–Shao–Tao–Teräväinen with ε = 1/10, restricted to a solution in the region exp((log n)^{5/6}) ≤ k ≤ n/2, with the radius exp((log log a)^{9/10}) taken without the implied constant (a smaller radius, so a weaker statement), and counted as rows n' rather than solutions (n', k'): a row of the half triangle holds a at most one column, so rows ≤ solutions ≤ 1. The paper's proof (its Section 2) is real analysis of the binomial coefficient as a function of its lower index; nothing of it is in Mathlib.
